hypothesis.falsifier: The patch passes the native MUL_MAT and MUL_MAT_ID scalar-reference fixtures for both Q4_K and Q5_K (activation widths 1-8, with the DSO specializations actually hit), yet a direct matched A/B on aggregate_tok_s (n>=5) fails to clear the decode floor 1.544% (prefill 0.973%) - i.e. the Q4_K X4_T kernel is DRAM-bandwidth-bound rather than instruction/load-port-bound and halving the 256-bit inner-loop instruction count cannot move aggregate throughput above the noise floor.
hypothesis.statement: The hot Q4_K dot kernel mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp:795; profiled specialization <DequantizerQ4K_AVX2,1> = 19.43% of sampled user cycles, Q4_K total ~25.35%, the largest addressable kernel) is hardwired to 256-bit: per 128-element weight sub-block it issues 2x32B loads + 4 and + 2 srli unpack, then per activation row 4x32B y loads + 4x _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 + 5 int adds (lines 838-865). The same file already contains a 512-bit sibling for the identical Q4_K/Q5_K dequantizer family against the Q8_K y-format (mul_mat_qX_K_q8_K_AVX512, lines 380-421, with zmm Q4Bits prepare64 + permute1/2 shuffles at lines 307-331), but no 512-bit variant exists for the Q8_2_X4 y-format that dispatch actually selects for Q4_K/Q5_K. Mechanism: add a #ifdef HAVE_FANCY_SIMD 512-bit inner loop to the Q4_K/Q5_K-only template body plus Q4_K/Q5_K-specific zmm nibble dequantizers (new structs mirroring the file's existing zmm Q4Bits idiom; the shared Q4Bits_AVX2 at line 754, also used by Q6_K, is untouched): per sub-block 1x64B weight load + 2 mask/shift unpacks, 2x64B y loads, 2x _mm512_dpbusd_epi32, 4-add reduction, with the existing float scale/min epilogue (d8 + scales[2] fmadd, lines 821-836/862-864) byte-for-byte unchanged. This halves unpack+dpbusd instructions and load instructions per weight byte on this AVX-512 Zen 4/5 host (avx512f/vl/bw/dq/vnni present in /proc/cpuinfo; GGML_NATIVE=ON -> HAVE_FANCY_SIMD defined). Integer dots are exact in int32 regardless of lane grouping (same 16-element partition, |sum| << 2^31) and the float epilogue is unchanged, so outputs are bit-identical; the dense path streams at 176 GB/s = 83% of the 220 GB/s host read ceiling, so the ~17% residual gap on that path is the recoverable headroom if the ny=1 256-bit inner loop is load-port/issue-bound.
